The '''Charter of Rights and Limitations''' was a constitutional document ratified in [[Imperial Suomi]] in 1850.

The source gives the charter's date and title but does not provide its clauses. The safest reading is that it became an important limitation on older royal government and later helped prepare the 1958 restructuring into a constitutional monarchy.

== Political Significance ==

The charter belongs to Suomi's gradual constitutional development rather than to a sudden revolution. It likely defined some combination of rights, legal procedure, and limitations on crown power, but those details should not be fixed until more canon exists.

By 1994, the charter remained part of the state's constitutional memory and one of the main historical anchors for the relationship between the [[House of Jarvinen]] and Suomi's representative institutions.
